objects.definition:
#if _WIN32
typedef std::wstring path_t;
#define PATHSTR(X) L##X
#else
typedef std::string path_t;
#define PATHSTR(X) X
#endif
objects.description: path_t is a platform-dependent alias for the filesystem path string type: std::wstring on Windows (UTF-16 wide string) and std::string on non-Windows platforms (UTF-8/locale-dependent narrow string). Use it for file and directory paths, along with PATHSTR() to create string literals with the appropriate character type.

functions.name: path_is_directory
functions.description: Returns true if the given path refers to an existing directory. On Windows, queries attributes with GetFileAttributesW; on POSIX, uses stat and S_ISDIR. Intended for quick directory checks before listing or opening paths.
requirements: Input path must be a valid path_t (std::wstring on Windows, std::string elsewhere).
The path is interpreted as-is (no normalization or expansion).
On POSIX, the path must be accessible to stat; lack of permissions or nonexistence yields false.

functions.name: list_directory
functions.signature: static int list_directory(const path_t& dirpath, std::vector<path_t>& imagepaths)
functions.description: Lists regular files and symlinks in the given directory and returns their names (not full paths) in imagepaths, sorted ascending. Clears imagepaths first. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure (and prints an error to stderr). Uses _wopendir/_wreaddir on Windows and opendir/readdir on POSIX.
requirements: dirpath must refer to a directory that exists and is readable by the process.
imagepaths is an output parameter and will be cleared at the start of the call.
Only entries with d_type == DT_REG or DT_LNK are included; other types (directories, sockets, etc.) are skipped.
Returned entries are bare names; the caller must prepend dirpath if full paths are required.
On failure to open the directory, the function returns -1 and writes an error message to stderr.

functions.name: get_file_name_without_extension
functions.description: Returns the substring of path before the last '.' character. If no '.' is present, returns the input unchanged. This is a simple string-based operation; it does not treat path separators specially and will also strip an extension from directory names if they contain a '.' in the string.
requirements: Input is treated as a generic string; only the last '.' is considered.
If the filename ends with '.', the trailing '.' is removed.
No validation of the path is performed; it need not exist.

functions.name: get_file_extension
functions.description: Returns the substring after the last '.' in path. If no '.' is present, returns an empty path_t. This is purely string-based; path separators are not considered, and hidden-file prefixes (e.g., '.bashrc') will yield the entire trailing portion after the leading dot as the extension.
requirements: Only the last '.' is considered as the separator between name and extension.
If the path ends with '.', the function returns an empty string for the extension.
No filesystem access is performed; the path need not exist.

functions.name: get_executable_directory
functions.description: Returns the directory of the current executable, including the trailing path separator ('\' on Windows, '/' elsewhere). Implementation is platform-specific: GetModuleFileNameW on Windows, _NSGetExecutablePath on macOS, and readlink("/proc/self/exe") on Linux/other POSIX.
requirements: No input parameters.
The returned path includes a trailing separator; callers should avoid adding an extra separator when concatenating.
Behavior depends on platform-specific facilities; on some systems long paths may be truncated due to a fixed 256-byte buffer in this implementation.

functions.name: filepath_is_readable
functions.description: Returns true if the file at the given path can be opened for reading in binary mode. Uses _wfopen on Windows and fopen elsewhere; closes the file immediately on success.
requirements: Input must be a valid path_t string representing a file path.
The check reflects current read permissions and file existence at the time of the call.
Directories or special files that cannot be opened as regular files will return false.

functions.name: sanitize_filepath
functions.description: If the given path is directly readable, returns it unchanged. Otherwise, returns get_executable_directory() concatenated with path. Intended to resolve resources located next to the executable when a relative path isn't directly resolvable.
requirements: If path is not readable, the function performs a simple string concatenation: returned value is get_executable_directory() + path, with no insertion of a separator.
Callers should ensure path is a relative name appropriate for concatenation, or include the needed separator if necessary.
Relies on filepath_is_readable and get_executable_directory behaving correctly on the current platform.
